Thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned on the data residency / region-pinning items you flagged: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Scope: models will be used for customer support NLP and document processing (some documents contain PII: names, account numbers).
- Need: EU-only storage for EU customers, US-only for US customers; ability to pin tenants/teams to region.
- Failover: you asked how cross-region failover works and whether backups or logs cross borders by default.
- Encryption/KMS: you asked about customer-managed keys and HSM support for Private deployments.

Open questions we promised to follow up on: 
1) Can we guarantee no data (including backups or logs) leaves the pinned region unless explicitly enabled?
2) What is the cross-region failover behavior (automatic failover vs manual failover) and typical RTO/RPO?
3) How are audit logs and request/response logs handled (retention, redaction, ability to store/export to your SIEM)?
4) Backup replication: are backups replicated across regions by default, and can that be restricted to a single region?

What I’m attaching: redwood-region-pinning-overview.pdf (short tech note) and a draft SOW template for the scoped deployment (acme-multiparty-sow.docx).

Next steps proposed:
- Aditya to provide technical answers to the questions above and share any compliance docs.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive next week with your infra/security team to validate assumptions (30–45 min).

If you can confirm the list of datasets that should be EU-only vs US-only that would help us prepare the deep-dive.

John / Susan —

Thanks — I took the action to share concrete details below. High level: Redwood supports per-tenant region pinning and configurable cross-region replication. We can meet all the constraints you listed, but some behaviors are configuration choices (not defaults) to satisfy strict residency/legal controls.

Short answers to your bullets: 

1) Data egress / backups/logs crossing region:
- By default, for "region-pinned" tenants we keep primary datastore, backups, and request logs in the pinned region. Cross-region replication is an opt-in configuration (disabled by default for region-pinned tenants).
- If cross-region replication is enabled for high-availability, it can be restricted to jurisdictions you approve (e.g., EU-only).

2) Failover behavior (automatic vs manual) & RTO/RPO:
- Two common deployment patterns: active-standby (recommended for strict residency) and active-active (recommended where low-latency global access is needed).
- Active-standby (cross-region standby): failover can be automated with RTO typically 5–30 min depending on session/kv-cache size and network warmup. RPO depends on replication frequency; we can target sub-hour RPO (1 hour or less) with asynchronous replication tuned for your workload.
- Active-active: requires cross-region replication of state and will involve cross-border data movement unless confined to multiple data centers within the same jurisdiction. We do not enable cross-border replication for EU-pinned tenants unless explicitly configured and accepted by legal.

3) Backups:
- Backups for region-pinned tenants are stored in the same region by default. We support customer-managed retention and encryption policies. Cross-region backup replication is available but off by default for compliance reasons.

4) Audit & request logs:
- Request/response logging that could contain PII is stored in the tenant region and can be configured to be redacted or routed to your customer log sink (S3, GCS, or your SIEM) in the same region.
- Audit logs (control plane) can be exported on demand and are available with configurable retention.

5) Encryption / KMS:
- In Redwood Dedicated and Private, you can use customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM-backed key stores. For Hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) in select enterprise plans.

Related docs: 
- Region pinning design note: https://redwood.ai/docs/region-pinning
- Example KMS integration guide (internal): https://redwood.ai/internal/kms-integration (we can share a redacted copy)
